extracted.intended_audience: national industrial-design/patent offices, WIPO staff, IP attorneys and administrators involved in design registration and classification
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and explanatory notes for classifying industrial designs under the Locarno Agreement (WIPO), including structure of the classification, numbering and notation conventions, procedural rules for amendments, and guidance for offices on use in deposit/registration documents and publications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Components of the International Classification
rubrics_metrics.description: The international classification shall comprise: (i) a list of classes and subclasses; (ii) an alphabetical list of goods in which industrial designs are incorporated, with an indication of the classes and subclasses into which they fall; (iii) explanatory notes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the mandatory three-part structure of the Classification (Article 1(3)).

rubrics_metrics.name: List of classes and subclasses (annexed list, subject to amendment)
rubrics_metrics.description: The list of classes and subclasses is the list annexed to the Agreement, subject to such amendments and additions as the Committee of Experts may make to it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The annexed list (31 classes) is the baseline; changes require Committee procedure (Article 1(4)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative character and national legal scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject to the requirements prescribed by this Agreement, the international classification shall be solely of an administrative character; nevertheless, each country may attribute to it the legal scope which it considers appropriate; the international classification shall not bind the countries as regards the nature and scope of the protection afforded to the design.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Classification is intended for administrative use — any legal effect is determined by national law (Article 2(1)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of class/subclass numbers in official deposit/registration documents and publications
rubrics_metrics.description: The Offices of the countries of the Special Union shall include in the official documents for the deposit or registration of designs, and, if they are officially published, in the publications in question, the numbers of the classes and subclasses of the international classification into which the goods incorporating the designs belong.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offices are required to indicate classification numbers on official forms and publications to facilitate retrieval and international consistency (Article 2(3)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Languages and authenticity of texts
rubrics_metrics.description: The international classification shall be established in the English and French languages, both texts being equally authentic; official texts in other languages may be established by the International Bureau after consultation with the interested Governments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: English and French versions are authoritative; translations may be made official following consultation (Article 1(7), Preface V).

rubrics_metrics.name: Alphabetical list structure and duplication under multiple key-words
rubrics_metrics.description: The alphabetical list consists of two parts: a first part comprising, in alphabetical order, all the goods whatever the class and subclass to which they belong, and a second part in which the goods are arranged alphabetically according to classes and subclasses; the same goods may appear several times under different key-words.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To facilitate consultation the same goods may be listed multiple times under various key-words; the list uses two complementary alphabetical arrangements (Preface IV).

rubrics_metrics.name: Choice of key-words (avoid over-broad generic headings)
rubrics_metrics.description: In choosing key-words, words in very frequent use, such as 'machines,' 'apparatus,' 'instruments,' 'utensils,' and 'devices,' which would have entailed grouping too many goods under one single heading, were disregarded; e.g., 'sewing machines' should be looked for under 'sewing machines' and not under 'machines (sewing-)'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use specific entries rather than broad generic terms so as to avoid excessively large headings and improve findability (Preface IV).

rubrics_metrics.name: Explanatory notes placement and consultation
rubrics_metrics.description: The explanatory notes have not been published separately but appear after the text of the class or subclass to which they refer; notes relating to a class are not repeated in the subclasses which they concern — it is advisable to consult them together.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Users should consult class notes alongside subclass notes because class-level notes apply to multiple subclasses (General Note / Preface IV).

rubrics_metrics.name: Numbering and notation format (recommended)
rubrics_metrics.description: The class number is indicated in Arabic figures; the subclass number is also indicated in Arabic figures, but it must always contain two digits (numbers 1 to 9 preceded by an O); the class number is separated from the subclass number by a dash (for instance: Class 1 Subclass 4 indicated thus: 1-04). The class and subclass numbers will be preceded by the indication 'Cl.' (for instance: Cl. 1-04).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formal recommendation to offices on exact formatting and leading-zero convention for subclasses (Recommendation (a) and (b)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Notation for multiple classes/subclasses
rubrics_metrics.description: If the numbers of several classes or subclasses must be indicated for one and the same deposit, the classes should be separated by a semicolon and the subclasses by a comma (for instance: Cl. 8-05, 08; 11-01).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides standard punctuation to list multiple classifications on a single deposit/record (Recommendation (c)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection of terms with respect to exclusive rights
rubrics_metrics.description: In selecting terms for inclusion in the alphabetical list of goods, the Committee of Experts shall exercise reasonable care to avoid using terms in which exclusive rights may exist; the inclusion of any word, however, is not an expression of opinion of the Committee as to whether or not it is subject to exclusive rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Committee should avoid terms that imply or conflict with proprietary rights, but inclusion does not evaluate trademark/patent status (Article 2(4)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Committee of Experts: composition and competencies
rubrics_metrics.description: A Committee of Experts shall be entrusted with finalizing the list of classes and subclasses, adopting the alphabetical list and explanatory notes, and keeping the International Classification up to date; each country of the Special Union shall be represented on the Committee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Committee prepares, adopts and maintains the Classification and its explanatory material (Article 3(1), Preface III).

rubrics_metrics.name: Committee decision-making and voting thresholds
rubrics_metrics.description: The Committee of Experts shall adopt the alphabetical list and explanatory notes by a simple majority of the votes of the countries of the Special Union; decisions to adopt amendments and additions shall be by simple majority, but if such decisions entail the setting up of a new class or any transfer of goods from one class to another, unanimity shall be required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Simple majority for ordinary amendments; unanimity for creation of new class or class transfers (Article 3(2), 3(4)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposals for amendments: who may propose and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals for amendments or additions to the international classification may be made by the Office of any country of the Special Union or by the International Bureau; proposals shall be transmitted by the International Bureau to Committee members not later than two months before the session at which they are to be considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formal submission channels and advance notice requirement (Article 3(3)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Mail voting and deemed acceptance
rubrics_metrics.description: Each expert shall have the right to vote by mail. If a country does not appoint a representative for a given session, or if its appointed expert has not expressed his vote during the session or within a period to be prescribed, the country concerned shall be considered to have accepted the decision of the Committee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides for absentee/mailing procedures and consequences of non-participation (Article 3(5)-(6)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Entry into force of Committee decisions and special six-month rule
rubrics_metrics.description: The alphabetical list, explanatory notes and any amendment or addition adopted by the Committee shall be communicated to the Offices by the International Bureau and shall enter into force as soon as the communication is received; nevertheless, if such decisions entail setting up a new class or any transfer of goods from one class to another, they shall enter into force within a period of six months from the date of the communication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Immediate effect for most amendments; six-month delay required for structural class changes to allow adaptation (Article 4(1)).

rubrics_metrics.name: International Bureau responsibilities for publication and incorporation
rubrics_metrics.description: The International Bureau, as depositary of the international classification, shall incorporate amendments and additions which have entered into force and shall communicate them to Offices; announcements of amendments and additions shall be published in the periodicals to be designated by the Assembly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bureau acts as repository and publisher of official updates (Article 4(2)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Superiority principle for ordering subclasses
rubrics_metrics.description: The various subclasses have been established according to the so-called 'superiority principle,' which means that each class begins, as far as possible, with the most restrictive subclass and ends with the most general.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subclass ordering should go from narrow (restrictive) to broad (general) to aid specificity (Preface III).

rubrics_metrics.name: Number and table of classes
rubrics_metrics.description: The list of classes consists of 31 classes; a table of classes (without subclasses) is provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: High-level organization: 31 top-level classes enumerated (Preface / Table of Classes).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use as principal or subsidiary system (national discretion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each of the contracting countries has the right to use the International Classification as a principal or as a subsidiary system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: National offices may adopt the Classification as their primary classification or keep it as an auxiliary reference (Preface / Article 2(2)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Assembly governance, quorum and voting (for the Special Union)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Special Union shall have an Assembly consisting of member countries; each country has one vote; one-half of the countries constitute a quorum; decisions of the Assembly generally require two-thirds of the votes cast; the Assembly deals with maintenance, development, budget, official texts in other languages, and may establish committees and working groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes higher-level governance and voting thresholds for matters concerning the Special Union (Article 5).

rubrics_metrics.name: Alphabetical list key-word selection rule about frequent words
rubrics_metrics.description: To facilitate consultation of these lists, the same goods may appear several times under different key-words. In choosing the key-words, words in very frequent use, such as 'machines,' 'apparatus,' 'instruments,' 'utensils,' and 'devices,' which would have entailed grouping too many goods under one single heading, were disregarded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit rule to avoid extremely common umbrella words as key-words to improve lookup granularity (Preface IV).
